title: Tidying up and helping out
keyIdea: Helping means doing small jobs that make things better for everyone: putting toys back in their own home, setting out a cup for each person, giving a pet its own dinner and water. We tidy so things can be found again and so no one trips. Good helpers ask "Can I help?" and pick a job that is the right size, leaving sharp, hot and heavy jobs to grown-ups.

kid: Every toy has a home. Blocks go in the toy box. Books go on the shelf. Coats go on the peg. When we put things back, we can find them next time.
Toys on the floor can trip us. Ouch! A tidy floor keeps everyone safe. Pushing toys under the sofa is not tidy. Put them in their home.
You can help at home. Set out one cup for each person. Give the dog her own dinner and some water. Wash the carrots with Gran.
Ask, "Can I help?" Pick a small job. Sharp knives, hot pans and heavy bags are for grown-ups. When we all help, the job is quick and everyone is happy.
adult: Development Matters (2023) covers this in Personal, Social and Emotional Development. At 3 and 4, children develop their sense of responsibility and membership of a community. They also become more independent in meeting their own care needs. Small jobs lead on to the Managing Self early learning goal at the end of Reception.

Children tidy best when each thing has one clear home, with a picture label on the box or shelf. Say the reason out loud: so we can find it, so no one trips. Setting a cup for each person is early maths too. It uses one-to-one correspondence. Real jobs done next to an adult build more pride than praise alone.

Common mistakes: redoing the job straight away, so the child learns their help is not wanted. Letting 'tidy' mean hiding things. Offering jobs that are too big, sharp or hot. Be careful with pets. Chocolate, grapes and raisins are poisonous to dogs. Children give only the pet's own dinner, and an adult measures it.

In the lab your child puts six things in their homes, and finds that under the sofa is refused. They clear four toys so Teddy can walk to the door without tripping. They set one cup for each of four people. They give Pip her dinner and water but not chocolate. Then they pick kind jobs of the right size in three helping scenes.

familyTip: Give each kind of toy one home with a picture on the box. At tidy-up time, say the reason ("so no one trips") and work alongside your child for the first few minutes, then let them finish one small job alone and leave it as they did it.

visual.caption: A small job for me, or a job for a grown-up? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: feeding the fish with a grown-up

lab.caption: Flagship lab: put things in their homes, clear the path so no one trips, set a cup for each person, feed the dog safely and pick a right-sized helping job.

practice.prompt: Tidy up time! Where does a book go?
practice.hint: Where can you find it next time?
practice.explain: Books go back on the shelf. Then you can find them, and no one steps on them.

practice.prompt: There are {n} toys on the floor. You put them all in the toy box. How many toys are in the box?
practice.hint: Count each toy as you put it in.
practice.explain: You put in every toy, so {n} toys are in the box. The floor is clear.

practice.prompt: Why do we tidy toys off the floor?
practice.hint: What can happen if you step on a toy?
practice.explain: Toys on the floor can make someone trip and fall. Tidying keeps everyone safe.

practice.prompt: {n} people sit down for snack. You give one cup to each person. How many cups do you need?
practice.hint: One cup for each person. Count the people.

pool.prompt: What can Pip the dog eat?
pool.hint: Some of our treats make dogs ill.
pool.explain: Dogs eat dog food. Chocolate and sweets can make a dog very poorly.

pool.prompt: Dad has lots of heavy shopping. What do you say?
pool.hint: Good helpers ask before they jump in.
pool.explain: "Can I help?" is kind. Dad can give you a small bag to carry.

pool.prompt: There are {n} blocks on the floor. Mia puts {k} in the box. How many are still on the floor?
pool.hint: Take away the ones Mia put in the box.
pool.explain: {n} take away {k} leaves {=n-k} blocks on the floor. Keep tidying!

pool.prompt: Which job is right for you?
pool.hint: Which one can not cut or burn you?
pool.explain: Washing carrots is safe. Sharp knives and hot pans are grown-up jobs.

pool.prompt: Your friend spills juice. What do you do?
pool.hint: What would make your friend feel better?
pool.explain: Helping wipe it up is kind and makes the mess go away fast.

pool.prompt: You push all the toys under the sofa. Is that tidy?
choices: No, they need to go home
pool.hint: Can you find them next time?
pool.explain: Hidden is not tidy. Toys go back to their own home so we can find them.

pool.prompt: Four children each have one cup. {n} more friends come. How many cups now?
pool.hint: Start at 4 cups and count on one for each new friend.
pool.explain: 4 and {n} more makes {=4+n} cups, one for each child.

pool.hint: Can small hands lift a toy?
pool.explain: Everyone can help, even little ones. When we all help, it is done fast.
